physiology.note: The 'medical' physiology model (M10.1), on top of core/wounds.json physiology (owner clock of 2026-11-11, unchanged). Research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only. Tension pneumothorax: 3-4 % of the fatally wounded, 15 of 26 lived long enough to reach a medic (J Trauma 2006, medium); the chance per penetrating chest wound (0.15), onset 5-30 min and death 10 min after onset are game values. Head injury: some conscious head wounds pass out after a lucid interval of 2-30 min (game values). Broken bones: 35 % of limb wounds of severity 0.25 or more (game value). Burns lose plasma (Parkland formula: about 4 ml per kg per % body surface per day; 0.0003 l/s per unit of burn severity, game value). Fluids: 500 ml run in over 10 min, 70 % of it counts as circulating volume (game value). Hypothermia: about twice the mortality, below 32 C core almost always fatal in trauma (Hypothermia Prevention CPG 2012, medium); a man in shock at 15 C air cools about 2 C an hour, wet x2, wind up to x1.5, aboard x0.3, wrapped x0.2 (game values); below 35 C clotting is twice as slow and every degree lowers the lethal blood loss by 3 points; out below 31 C, dead at 28 C. Tourniquet clock: no limb lost within 2 h (Kragh et al., J Trauma 2008, medium); amputation chance rising to 0.5 at 6 h and 0.9 at 10 h (extrapolation, low; owner to review).

levels.note: Medical jobs (owner 2026-11-14): first responder (Einsatzersthelfer B, strelok-sanitar), medic (Sanitaeter), stretcher bearer (riflemen tasked by the platoon leader: buddy-level skill), ambulance crew (medic level). A role may narrow what it is trained for (roles.json medical.interventions; owner Q-1b).

interventions.note: Research 2026-11-14 (search extracts only): experienced appliers about 25 s, inexperienced 28-38 s (JSOM 2025); self-application 3-8 s slower and 9-22 % less effective (Am J Transl Res 2021, PMC8290695); IDF field data 22 % failed to occlude, non-medical personnel fail often. Self-aid succeeds at the buddy chance times selfFactor. Care under fire: the only treatment allowed (TCCC), 1.3x slower (game value). Picks within the ranges are game values.
Re-check and tighten a tourniquet: tourniquets lose pressure within about 2 minutes of being applied, non-elastic straps especially (JSOM 2020, search extract). Time and success are game values.
Emergency (Israeli) bandage, Verbandpaeckchen, IPP-1. No measured time found in search extracts; times, success and the effect (bleeding x0.15) are game values.

Pack with haemostatic gauze (up to about 90 s) then hold pressure 3 minutes (JEMS 'Wound packing essentials', TCCC neck-wound guidance; search extracts). About 90 % haemostasis where haemostatic gauze is used (JEMS). Packing time and the success picks are game values.
Recovery position, sitting up, chin lift. No timing found; game values.
Nasopharyngeal airway. TCCC skill sheets list the steps, no time; Einsatzersthelfer B trains airway care (bundeswehr.de, search extract). Times and success are game values.
Vented chest seal. TCCC module 8 lists steps, no time. A tension pneumothorax may still develop and then needs decompression. Game values.

Failure 58 % in one series (J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2012), 3.2 cm catheters fail up to 65 %, about 80 % success with 5 cm catheters (reviews; search extracts). Einsatzersthelfer B trains airway relief (owner Q-1b: per national training). Times are game values.

IV versus IO 77 vs 83 s median (Cureus 2025 via ivteam.com); IV first attempt 46 % in hypovolaemic shock against IO 100 % (search extracts). stressFactor here stands for 'in shock'. Picks are game values.
FAST1 sternal 62-67 s (Hartholt 2010); FAST1 72-73 %, EZ-IO 87 % first-attempt success (field trial; search extracts). Picks are game values.
Hang a 500 ml bag on an access already placed: the time is connecting it; it then runs in over about 10 minutes (physiology fluidLps). TCCC prefers blood, which a platoon does not carry. Game values.
TCCC tablet pack (meloxicam and paracetamol), onset reassessed at 15 minutes (Ranger Medic Handbook 2025; search extract). Time and the relief are game values.
Opioid autoinjector or syringe tube (the Russian kit holds a promedol syringe tube, nordsint.org; fentanyl lozenge in TCCC). Time and relief are game values.
Ketamine 0.5 mg/kg IM or IN, repeat every 30-60 min (Ranger Medic Handbook 2025, search extract). Medics only. Time and relief are game values.
Rescue blanket or hypothermia prevention kit; hypothermic casualties have about twice the mortality (Hypothermia Prevention CPG 2012, search extract). No time found; game values.
SAM or improvised splint. Nothing found in search extracts; game values.
Replace a tourniquet with a pressure dressing (TCCC; medics only, within 2 hours). Game values.

carry.note: Walking wounded, unaided: about 60 % of a walk (leg wounds slow him further through the wound effects). Game value.
Arm over a comrade's shoulder. Game values.

One-man drag by the vest handle: 110 kg over 20 m in about 27 s by fit civilians (0.74 m/s); British Army standard 110 kg 20 m within 35 s (Vine et al., Applied Ergonomics 2023). A soldier in kit is about 105 kg. Endurance and rest are game values.
Two-person drag studied by Vine et al. 2023 (times not in the extract). Game values.
Fireman's carry: exposes both men upright (TCCC and US manuals advise a drag under fire). Speed and endurance are game values.
Two-man seat or fore-and-aft carry; two-person hand carry of a litter lasts about 3 minutes to exhaustion (1994 stretcher study, search extract). Game values.

Four-man litter: 4.8 km/h on a treadmill (1.33 m/s), proposed 1.0 m/s over ground; continuous carry up to about 5 minutes with harness (stretcher studies, search extracts); 30-60 s to unfold and load. Game values.

chain.note: Bundeswehr 10-1-2 rule: life-saving bleeding control and airway within 10 minutes, a doctor (Role 1) within 60 minutes, surgery within 2 hours (bundeswehr.de 'Rettungskette', search extract).

protection.note: Law: medical personnel, transports and men hors de combat are protected while they commit no acts harmful to the enemy (CIHL rules 25, 29, 47; GC I art. 19, 21, 22, 24). The numbers are game values (none published): an emblem on a vehicle recognised to about 300 m by eye and 800 m with optics, an armband to 50 m / 150 m, x0.3 in smoke or at night; a deliberate breach 1 % per decision, x3 after own losses, x2 for poor discipline, x2 when panicked (owner answer 5: from unit quality, stress and losses only, never from faction); a medic who fights loses protection for 120 s after his last shot.

triage.note: Chance of a wrong triage category (SPEC 9.1: sometimes wrong). Game values.
